cur-fossil-canadon-asfalto.dateNote: In the 1970s José Bonaparte dug Jurassic dinosaurs near Cerro Cóndor, Chubut, Argentina. In 1979 he named the long-necked Patagosaurus and the meat-eater Piatnitzkysaurus. The rock is about 180–168 million years old (Early–Middle Jurassic). Wikidata pins the formation at a rounded point.
cur-fossil-canadon-asfalto.summary: Jurassic rocks in Patagonia where Patagosaurus and Piatnitzkysaurus were found.

cur-fossil-la-colonia.dateNote: In 1984 José Bonaparte's team found an almost whole skeleton, with skin prints, in Chubut, Argentina. Named Carnotaurus in 1985, it is a horned meat-eater with tiny arms, about 70 million years old (Late Cretaceous). Wikidata pins the formation at a rounded point.
cur-fossil-la-colonia.summary: Where Carnotaurus, a horned meat-eater with tiny arms, was found with skin prints.
